Subject: Re: Severe latency and 503s from us-west-2 since 07:30 PT

Update (initial triage):
- Cloud provider reported host eviction in one AZ of us-west-2 starting 07:28 PT for a maintenance window + reactive draining. Several of our serving instances lost ephemeral local cache (KV cache) simultaneously.
- Smart routing immediately started redirecting traffic to other healthy AZs/regions. That traffic spike created transient token-throttling and connection churn on cross-region edges, which surfaced as 502/503s and high tail latency.
- We also saw long tails from re-warming the KV cache for model IO paths (increased disk I/O and queueing).

Immediate mitigations applied:
1) Pin routing policy for Apex to prefer regional failover (soft-fail rather than full cross-region overflow) to reduce cross-region bursts.
2) Temporarily raised per-customer concurrency and token rate limits for Apex to avoid throttling during failovers.
3) Bumped live pool size in adjacent AZs and enabled faster instance spin-up.

Current status: error rate dropped from 18% -> 4.6% in the last 15m; p95 latency improved but still above baseline (~420ms). Continuing to monitor. Asking cloud provider for exact maintenance/eviction timeline and whether further host drains are scheduled.

Next steps:
- Full postmortem after impact window; collect cache-priming timeline and routing logs.
- Consider deployment of cross-region smoothing (tokenized slow ramp) and warm standby priming for large customers.

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer

Jake — thanks for bearing with us and for the traces. Short note for your team that we can share with customers now: 

1) What happened: a provider-initiated host eviction in one AZ of us-west-2 caused simultaneous cache flushes for several of our serving nodes. Redwood's smart routing moved traffic out of the impacted AZ which temporarily surged traffic at cross-region egresses and produced transient 5xxs for some requests.

2) What we did: adjusted routing to soft-fail within the region to reduce cross-region overflow, increased concurrency and token rate limits for Apex, and accelerated pool scaling while we rewarm caches.

3) Next steps: Jonas will provide a full postmortem within 72 hours including cache rewarm timeline and concrete mitigations (smoothing + warm standby). We will offer a one-week pro-rata credit; Marcus will confirm numbers.
